headline: High: OpenBBTerminal’s broad egress and MCP/API surfaces create default data-leak and cascading-error risk when paired with a content-writing agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has broad network egress and is a content-writing agent, while B exposes MCP/REST/API surfaces and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible bridge where content from A can be fed into B as trusted instructions or vice versa. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF A’s output is copied into B’s MCP/API inputs without provenance checks
IF B parses text from A as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all A→B text handoffs
Disable automatic ingestion of free-form text into B
Use a fixed schema for A outputs before B consumes them
Review one sample A→B transfer for instruction-like content

B_data_leakage.rationale: B touches financial, licensed, and public data and can call APIs/MCP servers; A has broad network egress. Even without a shared filesystem, the pair can move sensitive material from B into A’s outbound context or outputs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF B sends financial or licensed data into A-generated text
IF A forwards B-derived content to external endpoints
mitigations: Restrict B inputs to non-sensitive datasets
Block A from receiving raw B workspaces
Redact financial/licensed fields before any handoff
Log and sample outbound requests from A for sensitive strings

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A’s profile shows no write or shell capabilities, while B explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. Overlap is mostly read/egress-oriented, so direct capability conflict is limited. Because B can use MCP and A can emit network traffic, a small coordination conflict remains possible, but not on shared mutable state.
conditions: IF an MCP server exposes shared mutable resources to B
IF A and B are both pointed at the same external API quota
mitigations: Assign separate API keys to each agent
Keep B on read-only MCP tools
Avoid shared mutable backends
Check for duplicate writes in one short test run

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing agent, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative text by B’s finance workflows. B has API/MCP access and can act on consumed inputs, making a mistaken A output capable of propagating into downstream work products. The profiles do not show explicit verification gates, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF B uses A’s text as source material without verification
IF B turns A-generated claims into reports, alerts, or API actions
mitigations: Require a human review step before B acts on A output
Force B to cite original sources, not A summaries
Mark A output as untrusted draft text
Run one end-to-end test with a deliberately wrong A claim

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly touches financial and licensed data and has documented secrets handling, while A has broad network egress. That combination can create retention or residency mismatches if B’s regulated data is summarized or transmitted by A. A is not itself a regulated finance tool, so this is a compliance-risk pathway rather than a direct violation.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is routed from B into A’s outbound context
IF A’s outputs are retained outside B’s compliance boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of A prompts
Document a retention rule for A-generated artifacts
Mask secrets before any B→A transfer
Verify residency and DPA coverage for any external endpoint
